machine.gpu: ANGLE (Apple, ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M1, Unspecified Version)

method: VITE_TEST_HOOKS=1 build served on 127.0.0.1:5206 (gzip for text types, no cache). Fresh browser context per viewport (desktop DSF 2; phone DSF 3, isMobile, hasTouch). Download = bytes the server sent from navigation until 2 s of network silence. States: first load, then each module tab (and its cinematic sub-state while a shot plays). Medium preset forced after the download measurement. Alive: two canvas-only screenshots 5 s apart, 3x3 grid, a region counts when >= 0.25% of its pixels change by > 12/255. Performance: 4 s sample per state; GPU time from EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 around each requestAnimationFrame dispatch; draw calls and triangles counted at the WebGL call level (all passes), max over the sample.

inspectableObjectsReach.note: Mouse, keyboard list and text mode checked at 1440x900, touch at 390x844, in every exploration state

exempt.reason: A dated front position along the valley path, not one object; the ice is drawn on the real DEM at 1 unit = 1 m.
The cliff is part of the drawn ice tongue; its height follows the illustrative ice thickness, so no size can be compared.
A crack pattern on the drawn ice surface (a texture), not separate objects.
Kilometres of drawn ice along the real valley; its size follows the DEM, which is at true scale.
High snowfields on the real DEM (true scale); no single object to measure.
A line on the real valley walls (DEM at true scale), not an object.
Bands of rock on the real valley floor and sides (DEM at true scale), not one object.
Rock peaks of the real DEM at true scale; no separate model.
Valley walls of the real DEM at true scale; no separate model.
The fjord itself, at true scale from the DEM; larger than any one view.
The sea surface over the whole scene; no size to compare.
Stream lines drawn on the real valley floor; their length follows the DEM.
A real glacier on the DEM at true scale, kilometres across; no separate model.
A real ridge of the DEM at true scale; no separate model.
A ground cover patch (a texture on the till), not a model with a size.
Cloud banks kilometres across; their size is illustrative.
The whole Copernicus DEM, about 32 by 44 km at true scale.
